Bilyy Kamin New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Bilyy Kamin's Jewish community, present from 1629, became independent in the late 17th century, reaching a peak of 1,901 people (54 percent of the town) in 1880 before a 1902 fire and the hardships of WWI drove it down to just 298 by 1921. In November 1942, the town's remaining Jews were deported to the Zolochiv ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, where they were murdered in 1943. This cemetery was demolished soon after WWII by new kolkhoz authorities, according to local residents, and the land used as a field; a monument was installed at the shooting site in 2005.
